newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudanese opposition asks Egypt to intervene.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese opposition asks Egypt to intervene.

text.p: The Sudanese opposition in exile, after earlier welcoming Egyptian neutrality, called on Thursday for Sudan's powerful northern neighbour to help overthrow the government in Khartoum.

The National Democratic Alliance (NDA), the umbrella organisation fighting the Sudanese army in the east and south of the country, repeated its defence of armed struggle against the Islamist-dominated military government.

"It (the alliance) calls on all Egyptian democratic parties and forces, and the Egyptian government, to stand with strength on the side of the people of Sudan and...help to speed up the liberation of Sudan from the government which has been oppressing it for eight years," its statement said.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has called the conflict between NDA rebels and the Khartoum government an internal affair, implying Egypt has no intention of intervening.
Egypt has not said it will help the rebels, despite its long dispute with the Sudanese government over the presence in Sudan of Egyptian Islamists fighting the Cairo government.

Egyptian opposition parties, reflecting an undercurrent of suspicion about the rebels, say they believe the offensive is part of an anti-Arab and anti-Moslem conspiracy to divide Sudan and control the Nile waters.
The Egyptian government's stock response to questions about its Sudan policy is that it opposes partition.
The NDA statement said it wanted Egyptian help to preserve the unity of Sudan "in the context of national, ethnic and cultural pluralism".

The opposition argues that the Islamist rulers, who took pwoer in a military coup in 1989, are the real danger to Sudanese unity because their approach to the long civil war in the south has completely alienated most southerners.
The NDA gave no details of the latest military developments in eastern Sudan, where the NDA says it has captured two border towns and a string of army garrisons.
The rebels last reported they were about 60 km (35 miles) south of the town of Damazin, site of the hydroelectricity plant which supplies most of Khartoum's power.
Their offensive began on the Ethiopian border on January 12. The Sudanese government says Ethiopian and Eritrean forces are doing most of the fighting but the other parties deny this.
